theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why should you ask a client about the skin-care products she uses at home before a facial?
options: So that you can tell her that all of her products are wrong
So you can copy her routine for the next client
To learn about her skin and spot products that may react
To find out how much money she spends every month

questions.stem: A client, Mrs Gordon, is 72 and takes medicine for high blood pressure. What should you do before her facial?
options: Record it and adapt the facial, with her doctor's advice if needed
Refuse to treat her, because clients over 70 cannot have facials
Ignore it, because medicine for blood pressure never affects the skin
Give her a strong heat treatment to help her blood flow

questions.stem: Which condition stops a facial completely and needs a referral to a doctor?
options: A few open pores on the nose
Mild dryness on the cheeks
Some blackheads on the chin
Impetigo (a skin infection)

questions.stem: What is the difference between a contraindication that 'prevents' a treatment and one that 'restricts' it?
options: One is found only on the face; the other is found only on the body
One stops the treatment; the other means you adapt it or avoid an area
There is no difference: both mean the client must go straight to hospital
A restricting one stops it; a preventing one has no effect on the service

questions.stem: A client has a small cut on her chin. What should you do?
options: Avoid the cut and work carefully around that area
Apply a scrub over the cut to clean it out well
Steam the cut for longer to help it heal faster
Put a clay mask over the cut to dry it out

questions.stem: When is the best time to carry out a detailed skin analysis during a facial?
options: Before taking off any of the client's make-up
After the mask has been left on the skin
After the cleanse, using a magnifying lamp
At the end, once the moisturiser is on

questions.stem: What is the difference between dry skin and dehydrated skin?
options: Dry skin lacks water; dehydrated skin lacks oil
Dry skin lacks oil; dehydrated skin lacks water
Dry skin is only found on men; dehydrated skin only on women
They are the same: both mean the skin has too much oil

questions.stem: Which signs usually show sensitive skin?
options: Thick skin with large pores and a lot of shine
An even colour all over, with a smooth and firm surface
Many blackheads across the forehead and nose
Redness that comes easily and tiny broken veins

questions.stem: What are comedones?
options: Small brown patches on the skin caused by the sun
Tiny broken red veins found on the cheeks and nose
Fine lines found at the outer corners of the eyes
Blackheads: pores blocked with oil and dead skin

questions.stem: Hyperpigmentation is common on deeper skin tones. What is it?
options: Patches of skin that are darker than the skin around them
Patches of skin that have become very oily and shiny all day
Small raised white bumps under the skin around the eyes
Skin that has lost all of its feeling after a bad injury

questions.stem: How should the facial couch be prepared for each new client?
options: Leave the towels from the last client in place if they still look clean
Spray it with perfume so that it smells fresh for her
Wipe it with disinfectant and cover it with fresh towels or couch roll
Cover it with the client's own clothes to keep it clean

questions.stem: What should you do with cotton pads and tissues once they have been used on a client?
options: Rinse them and dry them in the sun for the next client
Put them straight into a lined, lidded bin, ready to be emptied
Keep them on the trolley until the end of the day
Put them back in the clean cotton jar to save stock

questions.stem: Why should creams be taken out of their jars with a clean spatula?
options: So that the jar can be filled up with water
So that germs from fingers do not get into the jar
So that the product warms up before you use it
So that the client can see how much you have used

questions.stem: Why is a headband or turban put on the client before a facial?
options: To keep her warm during the whole treatment
To stop her from moving her head on the couch
To hide her hair so that she cannot see the mask
To keep the hair clean and away from the face

questions.stem: In what order should a client's make-up be removed in the first (superficial) cleanse?
options: Eyes and lips first, then the rest of the face and neck
Neck first, then the cheeks, and the eyes last of all
Only the face; eye make-up can be left on for the mask
Forehead first, then the eyes, then rub the lips firmly clean

questions.stem: Which cleanser usually suits an oily skin best?
options: A rich cleansing cream with heavy oils
A thick cold cream left on overnight
A foaming gel or light cleansing lotion
A cleansing balm made with cocoa butter

questions.stem: What is the main job of a toner after cleansing?
options: To remove the last traces of cleanser and refresh the skin
To add a coloured tint to the skin, like a foundation
To remove hair from the face before the mask is applied
To make the skin feel oilier so that the massage cream glides more easily

questions.stem: What does exfoliation do?
options: It adds oil to the skin to make it softer
It removes dead skin cells from the surface
It closes the pores so that they look smaller
It removes hair from the upper lip and chin

questions.stem: Which type of exfoliant is usually gentlest and best for sensitive skin?
options: A coarse scrub with large grains, rubbed hard
A rough cleansing sponge used firmly in small circles
A homemade scrub of sugar and lime juice
A mild enzyme exfoliant made for sensitive skin

questions.stem: Why is steam used during a facial?
options: To dry out the skin so that the clay mask sets much faster
To cool the skin down and close the pores up tightly
To warm and soften the skin and help to loosen blocked pores
To lighten the fine hair on the face so that it shows less

questions.stem: How should steam be used on a client with sensitive skin?
options: Closer to the face and for longer than normal
With a few drops of lime juice added to the water
Further away and for a shorter time, or not at all
Directly on the skin, with the nozzle almost touching

questions.stem: Before you turn the steamer towards the client, what should you check?
options: That it is giving off a steady stream of steam, not spitting water
That the water tank is completely empty so that it heats faster
That the client's eyes are wide open so that she can watch the steam rise
That the steamer is as close as possible to her face

questions.stem: Why should a magnifying lamp be covered when it is not in use?
options: To keep the bulb from getting too cold
To stop the lamp from using any electricity at night
So the client does not see her own skin
Sunlight through the lens can start a fire

questions.stem: How should you check a hot towel before it is placed on the client's face?
options: Hold it near your own face to feel the steam
Test it on the inside of your wrist first
Ask the client to touch it with her lips
Wave it in the air for about one second

questions.stem: Which massage movement is used to begin and end a facial massage?
options: Tapotement (light tapping)
Effleurage (smooth stroking)
Friction (small firm circles)
Petrissage (kneading)

questions.stem: In which direction should most facial massage movements go?
options: Downward and inward, towards the mouth
In any direction, as long as it is fast
Upward and outward, following the muscles
Downward only, from the forehead to the chin

questions.stem: Why should tapotement (tapping) be left out for a client with sensitive skin and broken veins?
options: It makes the massage cream dry out on the skin too fast
It is too slow and relaxing for this skin
It removes too many blackheads at once
It can make the redness and broken veins worse

questions.stem: Which type of mask is usually chosen for an oily skin with open pores?
options: A clay mask that sets and absorbs oil
A rich cream mask full of heavy oils
A warm oil mask left on for an hour
A thick honey and oil mask made for very dry skin

questions.stem: Which area should a setting mask NOT be applied to?
options: The centre of the forehead
The chin and jawline
The front of the neck
The eyes and lips

questions.stem: How is a clay mask removed at the end of its time?
options: Peel it off in one piece while it is dry
Soften it with warm damp sponges or mitts and wipe it away
Rub it off firmly with a dry towel so that none is left on the skin
Leave it on and tell the client to wash it off at home

questions.stem: Why should a daytime moisturiser with sun protection (SPF) be applied at the end of a facial?
options: The fresh skin needs protection from Jamaica's strong sun
SPF makes the skin oilier, and this is good for an oily skin
SPF removes the last of the mask from the skin
SPF stops the client from needing a facial again

questions.stem: A client's skin becomes very red, itchy and swollen soon after a mask is applied. What should you do?
options: Leave the mask on for longer so that it has time to do its work
Apply a second mask on top to calm the skin
Remove it at once with cool water and apply a cool compress
Massage the area firmly to spread the product in

questions.stem: Some mild redness of the skin after a facial massage is normal. Why?
options: The skin is having an allergic reaction to the cream
The client has caught an infection during the facial
The blood flow to the skin has increased for a short time
The skin has been burned by the cream used in the massage

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice should you give after a facial?
options: Go sunbathing on the beach that day to help the skin dry out
Avoid make-up and strong sun for the rest of the day
Use a strong scrub every day for the next week
Wash the face with laundry soap that night

questions.stem: Which daily home-care routine should you advise for most clients?
options: Cleanse, tone and moisturise twice daily, with SPF by day
Wash the face only once a week, with very hot water and soap
Use a coarse scrub hard on the face each morning and each night
Put only a thick body lotion on the face, and nothing else, at night

questions.stem: Which product is best for a client with a dry, flaky skin at the end of her facial?
options: An alcohol-based astringent toner
A clay mask left on to set hard
An oil-control gel with no moisture
A rich moisturiser for dry skin

questions.stem: A client, Odane, has razor bumps (ingrown hairs) in his beard area. Which approach is best during his facial?
options: Use gentle products and avoid harsh scrubbing over the bumps
Scrub hard over the bumps to pull out every ingrown hair
Pick out each of the bumps with a sharp needle to clear the skin fully
Steam the area for as long as possible at close range

questions.stem: Most salons allow about how long for a full facial, from start to finish?
options: About 10 minutes
About 4 hours
About 2 minutes
About 1 hour

questions.stem: Which room conditions suit a facial best?
options: A cold room with bright lights and loud music
A warm, quiet, clean room with soft lighting
A busy room near the front desk and the phone
A hot room with the windows shut and no air

questions.stem: Why should the therapist adjust the couch and stool height before a facial?
options: So that the client can see out of the window as she lies
So that the steamer fits under the couch
To keep her back straight and avoid strain
To make the room look tidier for photos

questions.stem: If blackheads are removed during a facial, which method is safest?
options: Squeeze hard with bare fingernails until they come out
Wear gloves and press gently with fingers wrapped in tissue
Use a pin to open every spot, including infected ones
Remove them before cleansing the skin, while it is still cold and dry

questions.stem: Which spots should never be squeezed during a facial?
options: Small open blackheads on the nose
Blackheads that come out with light pressure
Red, swollen spots that are infected
Blocked pores on the chin after steaming

questions.stem: Why should you write the products used and the client's reaction on her record card after the facial?
options: So the receptionist can work out her change
So the client can sell the products to friends
So that the card can be thrown away next week
So the next therapist can plan a safe treatment

questions.stem: A client asks which products to use at home. What should you recommend?
options: Products that suit her skin type and needs, with the price
The most costly products in the salon, whatever her skin
Whatever products the salon has the most of in stock
Products for a different skin type, to try something new

questions.stem: How should a facial be changed for a male client who shaves every day?
options: Use an extra strong scrub over the whole beard area, rubbing both ways
Work gently over the beard area, with the hair growth in mind
Apply a setting mask over the beard and leave it overnight
Shave his face first with a dry razor before cleansing

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What lamp is used to look closely at the client's skin during skin analysis?
Name the skin type that has neither too much oil nor too little, with a smooth, even surface.
What is the name of the massage movement in which you lift, squeeze and roll the muscles?
What is the name of the small, hard, white bumps of trapped skin cells, often found around the eyes and cheeks?
What do we call a mask that dries and tightens on the skin, such as a clay mask?
Name the fungal infection of the skin that shows as a red, ring-shaped patch.
What kind of water is normally used to fill a facial steamer, unless the maker says otherwise?
What do the letters SPF stand for on a moisturiser?
What is the name of the disposable paper roll used to cover the facial couch for each client?
What name is given to the forehead, nose and chin area, which is often the oiliest part of the face?
What is the medical word for redness of the skin caused by more blood flowing to it?
What is the name of the outer layer of the skin?
Which glands in the skin make sebum (the skin's natural oil)?

essays.stem: Describe how you would carry out a consultation and skin analysis before a facial treatment.
essays.modelAnswer: I greet the client, explain what will happen and fill in the record card with her. I ask about her medical history, medicines, allergies, skin-care routine, products she uses at home, any recent treatments, and what she wants from the facial. I check for contraindications. Next I remove her make-up and cleanse the skin, because make-up hides the true condition. Then I protect her eyes with damp cotton pads and look at the skin closely under a magnifying lamp. I note the skin type (normal, dry, oily, combination or sensitive) and any conditions, such as blackheads, open pores, dehydration, dark patches, broken veins or milia. I also feel the skin for texture and firmness. I explain what I found in simple words, agree a treatment plan and the products to be used, and write it all on the record card. The client signs the card before I start.
markingPoints: Asks about medical history, medicines, allergies, routine and goals
Checks for contraindications before starting
Cleanses first, then analyses the skin under a magnifying lamp with eyes protected
Identifies skin type and skin conditions
Agrees a treatment plan and records it, signed by the client

essays.stem: Explain the difference between contraindications that prevent a facial and those that restrict it. Give examples of each and say what you would tell the client.
essays.modelAnswer: A contraindication that prevents a facial means the treatment must not go ahead. Examples are skin infections such as impetigo, boils, cold sores, ringworm or conjunctivitis, a severe skin condition that is flared up, a fever, or recent surgery on the face. Infections can spread to the therapist and to other clients. A contraindication that restricts a facial means it can go ahead with changes, or with an area left out. Examples are a small cut or bruise, a few spots, a mild skin allergy, broken veins, recent sunburn on one area, or a medical condition such as high blood pressure, where heat may need to be reduced. If I find a preventing condition, I explain kindly that the facial cannot be done today, without naming an illness, and advise her to see a doctor. I record what I saw and offer to rebook once she is well.
markingPoints: Explains that a preventing contraindication stops the treatment
Gives correct examples that prevent (infections, severe skin conditions)
Explains that a restricting contraindication means adapting or avoiding an area
Gives correct examples that restrict (cuts, bruises, broken veins, blood pressure)
Refers tactfully without diagnosing, records it and offers to rebook

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare the treatment room, couch, trolley and client for a facial.
essays.modelAnswer: I make sure the room is clean, warm, quiet and private, with soft lighting and good air flow. I wipe the couch with disinfectant and cover it with fresh towels and couch roll, with a clean towel or blanket ready to cover the client. I set the couch and my stool to the right height so I can work with a straight back. I wipe the trolley with disinfectant and lay out clean bowls, sponges, spatulas, cotton pads, tissues and the products for her skin type, in the order I will use them. I check the steamer and magnifying lamp for damaged cables, fill the steamer to the line and place it safely. I put a lined, lidded bin near the trolley. I wash my hands. The client removes jewellery and upper clothing as needed, and I help her onto the couch, cover her with a towel for modesty and warmth, and put on a clean headband.
markingPoints: Room clean, warm, quiet and private, with suitable lighting
Couch disinfected, covered with fresh towels and couch roll, at the right height
Trolley disinfected and laid out in order with products for the skin type
Electrical equipment checked and placed safely; bin ready
Client prepared with care for comfort and modesty: jewellery off, covered, headband on

essays.stem: Describe how you would carry out the superficial cleanse and the deep cleanse in a facial, and how you would choose the cleanser.
essays.modelAnswer: The superficial cleanse removes make-up and surface dirt. I start with the eyes, using a gentle eye make-up remover on damp cotton pads, wiping from the outer corner inward under the eye and down the lashes on the lid. Then I clean the lips. Next I apply cleanser to the face and neck with light upward strokes and remove it with damp cotton pads or sponges. The deep cleanse comes after this. I apply the cleanser again and work it gently into the skin with small circles and upward movements for a few minutes, paying attention to the T-zone, then remove it fully and apply toner. I choose the cleanser for the skin type: a foaming gel or light lotion for oily or combination skin, a creamy cleanser for dry skin, and a mild, fragrance-free cleanser for sensitive skin. I keep products out of the eyes at all times.
markingPoints: Superficial cleanse removes make-up, eyes and lips first
Correct, gentle method around the eyes
Deep cleanse worked into the skin with suitable movements, then fully removed
Follows with toner
Chooses the cleanser to suit the skin type

essays.stem: Explain why exfoliation and steam are used in a facial, how you would use them safely, and how you would change them for sensitive skin.
essays.modelAnswer: Exfoliation removes dead skin cells, so the skin looks brighter and smoother and later products sink in better. A scrub works by rubbing gently with fine grains, and an enzyme exfoliant dissolves dead cells without rubbing. I avoid the eyes, any cuts and any spots, and I never rub hard. Steam warms the skin, increases blood flow and helps to loosen blocked pores before extraction or a mask. Before use, I check the steamer cable, fill it with water to the line as the maker says, and let it heat up with the nozzle turned away from the client until the steam is steady and not spitting. I cover her eyes with damp cotton pads and place the steamer at a safe distance, and I stay with her the whole time. For sensitive skin I use a very mild enzyme exfoliant or none, and I use steam further away and for a shorter time, or leave it out.
markingPoints: Explains the benefits of exfoliation
Explains the benefits of steam
Checks and pre-heats the steamer, nozzle turned away until steam is steady
Protects eyes, keeps a safe distance and stays with the client
Adapts for sensitive skin: gentler exfoliant, less or no steam

essays.stem: Describe the main facial massage movements and their effects, and say when you would change or leave out the massage.
essays.modelAnswer: Effleurage is a smooth, gliding stroke. It is used to begin and end the massage and to link the other movements. It relaxes the client and warms the skin. Petrissage is a kneading movement that lifts, squeezes and rolls the muscles. It improves blood flow and helps to tone the muscles. Tapotement is light, quick tapping with the fingertips. It stimulates the skin and is used on firm, healthy skin. Vibration is a fine trembling movement that soothes the nerves, and frictions are small circles that help to loosen tight areas. Movements go upward and outward, with even pressure and a steady rhythm, and I keep one hand in contact with the skin. I change or leave out the massage for sensitive skin and broken veins (no tapotement, lighter pressure), for active acne or spots (avoid the area), for swelling, bruising or recent injury, and when the client is unwell.
markingPoints: Effleurage: describes it and its effect
Petrissage: describes it and its effect
Tapotement and one other movement (vibration or friction) with effects
Upward and outward direction, even pressure and rhythm
Says when to change or leave out the massage

essays.stem: Compare setting and non-setting masks. Explain which skin types each suits and how you would apply and remove a mask.
essays.modelAnswer: A setting mask, such as a clay mask, dries and tightens on the skin. It absorbs oil, deep-cleans the pores and has a stimulating effect, so it suits oily and combination skin, and normal skin in a thin layer. A non-setting mask, such as a cream, gel or sheet mask, stays soft and moist. It soothes, hydrates and calms, so it suits dry, dehydrated, sensitive and mature skin. On combination skin I can use a clay mask on the T-zone and a cream mask on the cheeks. To apply a mask I take it out with a spatula and spread it evenly with a clean mask brush, working from the neck upward and avoiding the eyes, lips and nostrils. I place damp cotton pads over the eyes. I leave it for the time the maker gives and stay with the client. To remove it, I soften it with warm damp sponges or mitts, wipe it away gently, and then tone.
markingPoints: Setting mask: what it does and that it suits oily or combination skin
Non-setting mask: what it does and that it suits dry, sensitive or mature skin
Applies hygienically and evenly, avoiding eyes, lips and nostrils
Times it by the maker's instructions and stays with the client
Removes with warm damp sponges or mitts, then tones

essays.stem: What is a contra-action? Describe the contra-actions that can happen during or after a facial and what you would do for each.
essays.modelAnswer: A contra-action is an unwanted reaction during or after a treatment. Mild redness after massage or steam is normal and fades within a short time, but strong redness, itching, swelling or a rash may be an allergic reaction to a product. If this happens I stop at once, remove the product with cool water, apply a cool compress and, if it does not settle, advise the client to see a doctor. If a product gets into the eye, I rinse it with plenty of clean cool water and seek medical help if the eye stays sore. If the client feels faint or dizzy, perhaps from the heat of the steam, I stop, sit her up slowly, give her water and let her rest. A small burn from a hot towel or steam is cooled under cool running water and recorded. I write every contra-action on the record card and tell my supervisor.
markingPoints: Explains what a contra-action is
Allergic reaction: stop, remove the product, cool compress, refer if needed
Product in the eye: rinse with plenty of clean cool water
Feeling faint or a small burn: correct action
Records the contra-action and reports it to the supervisor

essays.stem: Explain the aftercare and home-care advice you would give a client after a facial, and why each point matters.
essays.modelAnswer: After a facial the skin is clean and more open, so I give advice to protect it. She should avoid make-up for the rest of the day, if she can, so the pores do not block. She should avoid strong sun, sea bathing in the heat of the day and heat treatments such as saunas for about a day, because the skin may redden and burn more easily. She should not touch or pick at her face, to avoid spreading germs. For home care, she should cleanse, tone and moisturise morning and night with products for her skin type, and use a sunscreen every day, because Jamaica's sun can darken patches and age the skin. She can exfoliate gently once or twice a week. She should tell me if any redness or itching appears. I suggest when to book her next facial, often in about four weeks, and I record the advice on her card.
markingPoints: Avoid make-up for the rest of the day, and why
Avoid sun and heat for about a day, and why
Do not touch or pick at the skin
Home-care routine: cleanse, tone, moisturise and daily sunscreen
Reports any reaction, rebooks and records the advice

essays.stem: Describe how you would work hygienically and safely during a facial, including the care of tools, electrical equipment and skin-care products.
essays.modelAnswer: I wash my hands before and after each client and keep my nails short and clean. I use fresh towels and couch roll for every client. I take products out with a clean spatula and close the lids at once. Sponges, cotton pads, spatulas and tissues are used once and put in a lined, lidded bin. Bowls and brushes are washed, then disinfected for the time the maker gives. I wear gloves for any extraction and put any used lancet or blade in the sharps box. I check plugs and cables before using the steamer or magnifying lamp, keep water away from electrical sockets, and never leave the steamer unattended near the client. I cover the magnifying lens when it is not in use. Products are stored in a cool, dry place with their labels, and are used before their expiry date. I follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules, and report any faulty equipment.
markingPoints: Hand washing, fresh towels and couch roll for each client
Hygienic product use and single-use items disposed of correctly
Bowls and tools cleaned then disinfected; gloves and sharps box used
Electrical equipment checked and used safely, magnifier covered
Products stored correctly; maker's instructions and Centre's rules followed

practical1.title: Cleanse, tone and moisturise facial with a skin analysis
practical1.brief: Work in pairs in the Centre's salon and take turns as therapist and client. In a group of five, one member works on a model who has agreed to take part. Each member prepares the couch and trolley, holds a consultation, checks for contraindications and completes a record card and a skin analysis chart. She then carries out a superficial cleanse, a deep cleanse, a skin analysis under the magnifying lamp, toning, a simple mask chosen for the skin type, and a moisturiser with sun protection. She gives her client aftercare and home-care advice. Each member also takes one job for the group: setting up the room, checking the electrical equipment with the assessor, taking the photos, or cleaning and disinfecting at the end. Photograph each stage below. Take close-ups of the work area only, with the client's eyes covered by damp cotton pads. Take a whole-face photo only if the client agrees in writing and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group, with the record cards and skin analysis charts.
materials: Clean towels, couch roll, headbands and blankets
Eye make-up remover, cleansers, toners and moisturisers with SPF for different skin types
Setting and non-setting masks, with mask brushes
Cotton pads, tissues, sponges, bowls and spatulas
Record cards and skin analysis charts
Salon disinfectant, gloves and a lined, lidded bin
photos: The couch and trolley set up, clean and laid out in order
Each member's record card and skin analysis chart (cover private details)
Superficial cleanse in progress: close-up of the eye area being cleaned
Deep cleanse being worked into the skin: close-up of one cheek
Mask applied evenly, avoiding eyes and lips, with eye pads on
The room and trolley cleaned and cleared
checklist: Washed hands and prepared the couch and trolley hygienically
Held a consultation, checked for contraindications and completed the record card
Removed eye and lip make-up gently and correctly
Carried out a thorough deep cleanse and removed all the product
Analysed the skin under the magnifying lamp and named the skin type correctly
Chose a mask and moisturiser that suit the skin type
Kept the client comfortable, covered and safe throughout
Gave correct aftercare advice and cleaned the area
safety: Do not treat a client with a skin or eye infection, open cut or rash: tell the assessor
Keep all products out of the eyes; if any gets in, rinse with plenty of clean cool water
Check plugs and cables before use, and keep water away from sockets
Cover the magnifying lens when it is not in use
Stop and remove the product if the skin becomes very red, itchy or swollen

practical2.title: Full facial with exfoliation, steam, massage and mask for a chosen skin type
practical2.brief: The assessor gives each member a skin type to plan for (oily, dry, combination or sensitive), and the member checks that her client's skin matches it, or changes the plan to suit the real skin. Work in pairs in the Centre's salon and take turns as therapist and client; in a group of five, one member works on a model who has agreed. Each member writes a short treatment plan and has the assessor check it. She then carries out a full facial: cleanse, skin analysis, exfoliation, steam (or a warm compress for sensitive skin), a facial massage of about 10 to 15 minutes using effleurage, petrissage and suitable other movements, a mask for the skin type, toning and moisturising. The group checks the steamer together with the assessor before it is used. Each member gives a home-care plan in writing. Photograph each stage below, as close-ups of the work area only, with the client's eyes covered. Take a whole-face photo only if the client agrees in writing and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Facial couch, stool and trolley, with towels, couch roll and headbands
Cleansers, toners, exfoliants (scrub and enzyme), massage cream or oil, masks and moisturisers for each skin type
Facial steamer with distilled water, and hot towels or warm compresses
Cotton pads, sponges, mitts, bowls, mask brushes and spatulas
Treatment plans, record cards and home-care advice sheets
Salon disinfectant, gloves and a lined, lidded bin
photos: The steamer checked and placed at a safe distance, with the client's eyes covered
Exfoliation in progress: close-up of one cheek
Massage in progress: close-up of the therapist's hand position
Mask applied for the skin type
The written home-care plan given to the client
The room, steamer and trolley cleaned and cleared
checklist: Wrote a treatment plan that suits the client's real skin type and needs
Checked and pre-heated the steamer safely and stayed with the client during steaming
Chose and used an exfoliant suited to the skin, avoiding the eyes
Massaged with correct movements, direction, pressure and rhythm
Applied and removed the mask correctly and hygienically
Adapted the treatment for the skin type (for example, less heat for sensitive skin)
Gave clear aftercare and a written home-care plan
Cleaned the steamer, tools and area as the maker and the Centre's rules say
safety: Pre-heat the steamer with the nozzle turned away from the client, and never leave it unattended
Test hot towels and compresses on the inside of your wrist before they touch the client
Cover the client's eyes with damp cotton pads during steam and masks
Wear gloves if any extraction is done, and never squeeze infected spots
Stop the treatment if the client feels faint or the skin reacts badly, and tell the assessor
